_meta.indication: VICTRELIS is a hepatitis C virus (HCV) NS3/4A protease inhibitor indicated for treatment of chronic hepatitis C (CHC) genotype 1 infection, in combination with peginterferon alfa and ribavirin, in adult patients (≥18 years) with compensated liver disease, including cirrhosis, who are previously untreated or who have failed previous interferon and ribavirin therapy.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing a boceprevir response-guided therapy (RGT) regimen of BOC/PR (28/48 wk) and BOC/PR (48 wk) to PR (48 wk), with a 4-week PR lead-in; randomization 1:1:1 in each of two cohorts.
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive adults with chronic HCV genotype 1 infection (previously untreated).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sustained virologic response (SVR), defined as undetectable HCV RNA (<10 IU/mL) measured 24 weeks after the end of therapy.
pivotal_trials.n: 1097 subjects received at least one dose (PR48 N=363, RGT N=368, BOC/PR48 N=366)
pivotal_trials.result: SVR 38% with PR48 control vs 63% RGT and 66% BOC/PR48; both boceprevir arms superior to PR (p<0.0001).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, parallel-group, multicenter study, double-blinded for boceprevir or placebo in combination with open-label PR; subjects randomized to 1 of 3 treatment arms.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with chronic HCV genotype 1 who failed prior peginterferon/ribavirin but demonstrated interferon responsiveness; classified as relapsers (n=259) or nonresponders (n=144); prior null responders excluded.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sustained virologic response (SVR), defined as undetectable HCV RNA (<10 IU/mL) measured 24 weeks after the end of therapy.
pivotal_trials.n: 403 subjects (PR48 N=80, RGT N=162, BOC/PR48 N=161)
pivotal_trials.result: SVR 21% with PR48 control vs 59% RGT and 66.5% BOC/PR48; both boceprevir arms superior to PR (p<0.0001).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>35% of subjects) were fatigue, anemia, nausea, headache, and dysgeusia. Anemia was more frequent with VICTRELIS combination (50% vs 30% in treatment-naive; 45% vs 20% in treatment failures); dose modifications due to anemia occurred twice as often (26% vs 13%).
target_moa: Boceprevir is an inhibitor of the HCV NS3/4A protease necessary for proteolytic cleavage of the HCV polyprotein; it covalently, reversibly binds the NS3 protease active site serine (S139) through an alpha-ketoamide group to inhibit viral replication.

advisory_committee.vote: The Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee was convened on April 27, 2011 and voted unanimously (18 yes, 0 no) for the approval of boceprevir.

description.text: Expanded the indication to include prior null responders to chronic hepatitis C genotype 1 treatment

citations.quote: VICTRELIS is approved for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C genotype 1 infection, in combination with peginterferon alfa and ribavirin, in adult patients (18 years of age or older) with compensated liver disease, including cirrhosis, who are previously untreated or who have failed previous interferon and ribavirin therapy. This supplement was submitted to expand the indication to include prior null responders.

description.text: Updated Clinical Studies and Microbiology-Resistance labeling with trial P06086 anemia management results (erythropoietin vs ribavirin dose reduction); no new indication added

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application provides for updates to the Clinical Studies Section 14, of the Package Insert (PI), with the results of clinical trial P06086, entitled, “Boceprevir and Peginterferon/Ribavirin for the Treatment of Chronic Hepatitis C in Treatment-Naive Subjects: A Comparison of Erythropoietin Use Versus Ribavirin Dose Reduction for the Management of Anemia.” In addition, the Microbiology-Resistance Section of the PI was updated with new information about the impact of specific amino acid substitutions on HCV replicon susceptibility to boceprevir.

description.text: Updated Clinical Studies section with final PROVIDE trial (P05514) report for genotype 1 chronic hepatitis C nonresponders to peginterferon/ribavirin

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application was submitted to update the Clinical Studies section of the Package Insert with the final study report for clinical trial P05514, entitled “A Single-Arm Study to Provide Boceprevir Treatment in Subjects with Chronic Hepatitis C Genotype 1 Deemed Nonresponders to Peginterferon/Ribavirin in Previous Schering-Plough Boceprevir Studies (PROVIDE).”

basis.text: The boceprevir NDA was given a priority review.

citations.quote: The boceprevir NDA was given a priority review and presented before an advisory committee meeting as discussed below.

summary.text: VICTRELIS (boceprevir) received Priority Review and the Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee, convened April 27, 2011, voted unanimously (18-0) for approval. FDA considered the SVR endpoint clinically validated, so the approval was a regular (traditional) approval and did not fall under accelerated approval regulations.
